text:
morgan: quick dump of a repro I hit during a drain: prefill committed residency while the original node still had an active lease. client retried and saw a tombstone.
neil: short trace pls
morgan:```
1) client read -> lease on nodeA
2) eviction triggers nodeB prefill
3) nodeA flips DEMOTED locally but lease not released
4) nodeB writes residency metadata believing demote==lease_release
5) client retry hits nodeA tombstone -> conflicting state
```
anya: this is the demote vs lease visibility gap. we need a guard so prefill doesn't make visible residency unless ownership is confirmed.
kevin: options: (1) make demote+lease release atomic (huge refactor), (2) epoch-guard CAS on prefill commit (small), (3) quiesce token handshake (optimizes aborts).
morgan: prefer (2) to ship fast: read lease_epoch E, attempt CAS when committing residency; on CAS fail abort and fallback to read-through.
neil: agree as first step. add backoff + cap retries so we don't thundering herd. also emit prefill_cas_failures metric.
anya: tests: unit CAS paths, integration sim with concurrent demote+lease race, and a canary with drain storm. I'll own tests.
kevin: impl notes: reuse generation-tagged writes for atomicity, write transient candidate keys with short TTL to avoid partial blobs. I'll draft a small PR `prefetch/epoch-guard-1781`.
infra-bot: scheduled canary: drain-storm-2025-05-10. tagging @morgan @kevin for verification.
morgan: thanks. we'll roll behind a feature flag, collect prefill_cas_failures and prefill_success_attempts. if abort rate high we'll prototype token flow. leaving thread open for follow-ups.
